learn.title: Compute: VMs, scale sets, availability sets, Azure Virtual Desktop
objectives: Compare virtual machines, containers and functions, and pick the right compute type.
Describe Azure Virtual Machines and when to use them.
Explain Virtual Machine Scale Sets and availability sets.
List the resources a virtual machine needs.
concepts: IaaS compute. You choose the image (OS), size (CPU and memory) and disks, and you manage the OS and everything on it.
A template containing an OS and, optionally, preinstalled software, used to create VMs.
The amount of vCPU, memory and other capacity a VM has. You can resize later (scale up or down).
Create and manage a group of identical, load-balanced VMs whose number can change automatically with demand (autoscale).
Spreads VMs across fault domains (separate power and network hardware, up to 3) and update domains (groups rebooted separately during maintenance, up to 20). No extra cost: you pay only for the VMs.
A group of VMs sharing a common power source and network switch, like a rack.
A group of VMs that can be rebooted at the same time during planned maintenance.
Desktop and app virtualisation in Azure. Users get Windows desktops and apps from any device, with Microsoft Entra ID security and multi-session Windows 11 or Windows 10 Enterprise.
A size, an OS disk (managed disk), a network interface in a subnet of a virtual network. Optionally data disks, a public IP and a network security group.
comparisons: VMs: full OS control, slowest to start. Containers: lightweight, portable app packages. Functions: event-driven code with no infrastructure to manage.
Scale set: many identical VMs that scale automatically. Availability set: protects VMs from rack failures and maintenance inside one datacenter.
Availability set: across racks in one datacenter. Availability zone: across physically separate datacenters in a region.
Scale up: resize a VM. Scale out: add VM instances (scale sets).
traps: Availability sets cost nothing extra. You pay for the VMs only.
Availability sets don't protect against a whole-datacenter failure. Zones do.
A public IP is optional for a VM. A network interface in a virtual network is required.
Azure Virtual Desktop is for end-user desktops, not for hosting websites.
With VMs you patch the OS. That's IaaS.
revision: Many identical VMs with autoscale → Virtual Machine Scale Sets.
Survive rack failure and planned maintenance → availability set (fault and update domains).
Cloud desktops for users on any device → Azure Virtual Desktop.
VM needs: size, disk, NIC, VNet/subnet; public IP and NSG are optional.
